subject: Service assurance addendum and evidence runbook — NuVita SOW/Order form
content:
From: Erica Lopez <elopez@nuvitahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nuvitahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Draft service addendum and evidence matrix for NuVita

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NuVita is excited to move toward a pilot. Attached is the latest SOW (NuVita_SOW_v1.2.pdf) and an initial Evidence_Matrix.xlsx that the procurement team asked us to complete. A couple of areas we need Redwood to confirm before we can route this to legal and procurement for signature:

- Uptime measurement: procurement wants explicit metrics for regional availability and a definition of what constitutes an availability incident. Can you confirm how Redwood measures availability for Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity?
- Latency windows: they prefer 95th and 99th percentile thresholds for 1s/3s buckets and want the exact sampling cadence used for reporting.
- Credits & remediation: proposed language around service credits and the cadence for credits needs to be in the order form exhibit.
- Evidence runbook: procurement requires a one-page runbook that explains what artifacts we will provide to validate incidents (logs, telemetry, SOC 2 references).

I attached the Evidence_Matrix with NuVita's initial asks. Can Redwood populate the right-hand columns and propose order form language for the uptime exhibit? James Park from our legal team is copied on questions about the MSA cross-references.

Appreciate a draft back by Friday if possible — procurement is aiming to close the pilot order by 11/5.

Best,
Erica Lopez
Head of Procurement, NuVita Health
Procurement Team: procurement@nuvitahealth.com

---

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Erica Lopez <elopez@nuvitahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft service addendum and evidence matrix for NuVita

Hi Erica — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. We reviewed the SOW and the Evidence_Matrix and sketched a companion addendum for the order form. Key points below; attached is a lightweight draft we think will cover procurement's needs (Redwood_Service_Assurance_Addendum_draft.docx).

Summary of our approach:
- Availability definition: We will measure availability per region using per-route health checks and token-level success rates aggregated over 1-minute windows and reported as rolling 30-day windows. An availability incident is defined as any 30-day rolling window where route-level success rate drops below the committed uptime (e.g., 99.9%).
- Latency SLOs: We'll provide 95th and 99th percentile tail latency tables for single-request generation and streaming calls. Sampling cadence: 1-minute buckets aggregated to hourly and daily reports; the order form will reference the 30-day rolling reporting window.
- Credits: Service credits will be calculated monthly as a percentage of monthly hosted usage fees, with a cap per month. For Dedicated customers we propose a graduated credit schedule tied to sustained degradation (see draft).
- Evidence runbook: We will supply incident timelines, per-route telemetry export, sampling of request IDs, and a SOC 2 snapshot. For on-prem/private deployments, evidence will be provided via a secure snapshot export and an on-site review option.

Open questions we need from NuVita to finalize the order form language:
1) Which routes will be in scope for the pilot (list of API route patterns)?
2) Estimated committed monthly tokens for hosted and dedicated usage so we can pick the right credit tiers.
3) Do you require automated DocuSign routing or will procurement handle manually?

Attachments in my reply: Redwood_Service_Assurance_Addendum_draft.docx (proposed exhibit), a populated Evidence_Matrix draft (partial), and a short template for the incident evidence export.

If that works, Karthik will produce a concise order form exhibit that you can feed to legal. I can also join a short call with procurement to walk through the runbook.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Erica Lopez <elopez@nuvitahealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@nuvitahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed order form exhibit language and evidence operations

Erica — following Irene's note I put together suggested order form exhibit language and an evidence operations checklist so procurement can see exactly what they'll receive. Extract below; full text is attached in the draft docx.

Proposed uptime exhibit excerpt:
- Committed Uptime (Regional): 99.9% monthly rolling for Hosted API. Dedicated capacity customers will have a per-pool uptime commitment of 99.95% and a regional failover commitment as defined in Section 3.2.
- Measurement: Availability is measured per route using 1-minute buckets of successful request rate, aggregated to 30-day rolling windows. Measurements exclude scheduled maintenance windows and customer-initiated maintenance per the MSA.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 900ms; 99th percentile <= 1.8s for single-request text generation on Hosted API. Streaming call latency SLOs are defined separately in Appendix B.
- Service Credits: In the event of a sustained availability breach (rolling 30-day below committed uptime), credits will be applied to the next invoice as follows: Tier 1 (99.9-99.0): 5% credit; Tier 2 (99.0-95.0): 15% credit; Tier 3 (<95%): 30% credit. Cap: 50% of monthly hosted charges.

Evidence operations checklist to be provided on incident request:
1) Incident start/end timestamps and route scope
2) Per-route 1-minute aggregation CSVs for the incident period (sampled)
3) Telemetry export: token-level error counts and server-side exception logs
4) Root cause notes and mitigation steps
5) SOC 2 report reference and snapshot (if requested)

We can populate the Evidence_Matrix with the exact artifact names and expected formats. Laura and I recommend adding a short clause that allows Redwood a 48-hour window to provide initial telemetry after a validated incident request to avoid blocking operational response.

Next steps: if procurement confirms the in-scope routes and token commitments, we'll finalize the exhibit and provide a DocuSign-ready SOW + exhibit package. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

---

From: Erica Lopez <elopez@nuvitahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <j.park@nuvi-legal.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@nuvitahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft service addendum and evidence matrix for NuVita

Thanks, Karthik and Irene — this is very helpful and much clearer for procurement. A few notes from legal/procurement after an initial pass:

- NuVita confirms the in-scope routes for the pilot: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/*, and embeddings endpoints. We'll send a short list of example route parameters by end of day.
- Procurement is fine with the proposed credit bands for Hosted API but would like a slightly higher cap for the pilot month only (propose 70% cap for pilot). Can you confirm you can accept that as a one-time exception?
- Legal asks for the SOC 2 snapshot plus a short explanation of how rolling windows are computed; James will redline the MSA cross-reference after he sees the finalized exhibit.
- DocuSign: procurement would prefer automated routing to the NuVita procurement mailbox. Please include the DocuSign initiation link in the final package.

I've attached an edited SOW PDF with a few minor scope tweaks (NuVita_SOW_v1.2_annotated.pdf). If you can push the finalized exhibit and evidence matrix back by Thursday EOD, we will route to legal and procurement and aim to sign next week.

Erica
Erica Lopez
Head of Procurement, NuVita Health
